chunks: Hanan, from Abu Al-Khattab, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him), who said:
The people were affected by severe drought during the era of Suleiman Bin Dawood (peace be upon them). So they complained about that to him, and sought from him that he should pray for rain for them.
So he said to them: 'When I have prayed the morning Prayer, I will go with you'.
So when he had prayed the morning Prayer, he went and they went (with him).

So when they were on one of the roads, there was an ant there which had raised its hand to the sky, and placed its feet upon the earth, and it was saying: 'Our Allah! We are also creatures from Your creatures, and we are not needless of Your sustenance, so do not destroy us for the sins committed by the children of Adam'.
So Suleiman (peace be upon him) said: 'Return! You shall be quenched by others (in other ways)'.
So they were quenched in that year the like of which they had never been quenched at all.
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the ant and rain during the time of Prophet Suleiman?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Sulayman (as) encounters an ant supplicating for rain, which serves as a profound lesson in Shia tradition on the efficacy of *dua* regardless of the supplicant's status. The event highlights the concept that divine mercy is not limited by hierarchy, as the humble prayer of a small creature can trigger the same cosmic response as that of a prophet. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of creation and the power of sincere devotion in invoking divine sustenance.
